# PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms

# PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.5.1 · generated 2026-11-27 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation recommends recording fatigue timing and its relationship to medication, evaluating non-PD causes such as anemia, pacing activity with breaks, regular exercise, and occupational-therapy advice on energy conservation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/fatigue
- [statement] PD-associated pain has heterogeneous syndromes, including musculoskeletal, dystonic, peripheral/radicular and central pain; describing the pain mechanism matters before choosing treatment. (medium confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2035-8377/12/3/14 · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26147660/
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review rated rasagiline efficacious but only possibly useful for fatigue, explicitly because the supporting positive trial was small and low quality; this is a historical rating, not proof of established long-term benefit. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation advises tracking fatigue in relation to medication timing and assessing other causes, including anemia, before attributing all fatigue to PD. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/fatigue
- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation recommends regular exercise, frequent breaks and occupational-therapy advice for energy conservation when managing fatigue. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/fatigue
- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation identifies convergence insufficiency as one cause of double vision and reduced blinking with dry eyes as one cause of blurry vision in PD. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/non-movement-symptoms

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A neuropathy review describes multiple potential contributors in people with PD, including genetic disorders, treatment effects and concomitant disease; its diagnostic approach includes history, clinical examination, blood tests and nerve-conduction studies. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847250/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] PD fatigue is a subjective lack of energy that interferes with function; it differs from sleepiness and from objectively measured muscle fatigability. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4883681/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/fatigue, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10473113/
- [statement] A review of Parkinson-related peripheral neuropathy lists diabetes, thyroid disease and B12 deficiency among acquired causes; sensory complaints therefore warrant assessment for peripheral neuropathy rather than automatic attribution to central PD pathology. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847250/
- [statement] Rotigotine showed numerical pain improvement in an exploratory placebo-controlled pilot, but the primary pain comparison was not statistically significant; MDS classified its PD pain use as investigational rather than established efficacy. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26626320/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] A single-center sham-controlled trial of motor-cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation reported a favorable musculoskeletal-pain signal in PD; its small sample and short follow-up support a preliminary adjunctive-treatment claim rather than broad efficacy across PD pain types. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32980772/
- [statement] The 2020 pain review distinguishes musculoskeletal, dystonic, nerve, primary and akathitic pain in PD; the heterogeneous pain presentation supports syndrome-specific assessment rather than a single analgesic strategy. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2035-8377/12/3/14
- [statement] A 2023 systematic review searching trials through May 2021 found a small fatigue benefit from physical exercise across eight trials, but called for further efficacy research and differentiation of physical versus mental fatigue outcomes. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10473113/
- [statement] In that 2023 review, pooled modafinil trials did not show a significant fatigue benefit versus placebo, and acupuncture did not show a significant advantage over sham acupuncture; these comparisons should not be presented as proven PD-fatigue therapies. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10473113/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Sensory symptoms in PD extend beyond pain: a 2023 review describes disturbances of vision, hearing, smell, taste, touch, temperature and position sense. This review-level observation does not establish a specific treatment for each disturbance. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37258441/
- [statement] For fatigue, the 2019 MDS review classified methylphenidate and modafinil as investigational with insufficient evidence; the Foundation likewise notes that the small positive methylphenidate trial needs further study. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/fatigue
- [statement] PANDA did not meet its primary pain endpoint at week 16. The 2019 MDS review accordingly found insufficient efficacy evidence for prolonged-release oxycodone–naloxone, despite a possibly useful practice rating based partly on its use for severe chronic pain outside PD. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26494524/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] In the 2024 OXYDOPA trial in parkinsonian central pain, neither prolonged-release oxycodone nor higher-dose levodopa demonstrated superiority over placebo. Adverse events leading to discontinuation were more frequent with oxycodone; the finding applies to this central-pain population. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38850081/
- [statement] Real acupuncture did not outperform sham acupuncture for PD fatigue in the Kluger and Kong randomized trials; a 2026 review likewise characterized fatigue evidence as very uncertain and without superiority over sham. Within-group improvement should not be presented as treatment-specific efficacy. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27028133/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5853635/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13189933/
- [statement] Small experimental studies found that levodopa can increase pain thresholds in PD. These laboratory threshold results should be distinguished from demonstrated relief of chronic clinical pain. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16078219/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2117570/
- [statement] Experimental findings on sensory thresholds conflict: one study reported that thermal and mechanical pain thresholds were uninfluenced by levodopa or STN-DBS, whereas another reported significant increases in mechanical pain and tolerance thresholds after acute STN-DBS and after acute levodopa administration. A uniform direct effect on central pain processing is not established by these studies. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20629160/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23864314/
- [statement] The 2020 review describes musculoskeletal pain associated with postural changes and muscular rigidity, including frozen shoulder, low back pain, arthritis and osteoporosis. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2035-8377/12/3/14
- [statement] In the 2015 PANDA trial, prolonged-release oxycodone-naloxone did not meet the primary pain endpoint in the full analysis population at week 16; the authors nevertheless considered the signal worthy of further research. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26494524/
- [statement] Sensory symptoms include diminished smell, which can precede PD diagnosis; the Parkinson’s Foundation notes that reduced smell can also reduce enjoyment of food and appetite. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/non-movement-symptoms
